title: AutoRFP vs Qvidian vs Arphie (2026): Legacy vs AI-Native RFP Tools
summary: AutoRFP vs Qvidian vs Arphie compared on formatted proposals, questionnaires, AI transparency, and the pricing model that will cost you most as you grow.
body_markdown:
Most AutoRFP vs Qvidian vs Arphie comparisons treat this as a three-way race. It isn't: Qvidian builds documents, while AutoRFP and Arphie answer questions.


**Key takeaways**


- **Qvidian is still the best document factory:** nothing here matches its Word templates and 70+ reports, but you pay in manual upkeep and a named seat per contributor.
- **AutoRFP is the fastest way off Qvidian for questionnaire-heavy teams:** it's the only one with published prices, and every user is included.
- **Arphie is the most transparent AI of the three:** it shows the source, confidence, and reasoning behind every answer, on a custom quote.
- **Inventive AI closes the gap all three leave:** it's an AI-native RFP platform that drafts cited answers from your connected company knowledge and flags conflicting or outdated content before it reaches a buyer, with formatted proposal output included.

## Do AutoRFP, Qvidian, and Arphie really compete with each other?


Only partly. Choosing between them means making two separate decisions.


- **Decision 1, legacy or AI-native:** Qvidian (owned by Upland Software) assembles approved content into branded Word proposals. AutoRFP (founded 2022) and Arphie (founded 2023) draft answers to hundreds of questions with AI.
- **When Qvidian still makes sense:** your output is mostly long narrative proposals, not questionnaires.
- **When it doesn't:** your week is[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/how-to-answer-a-security-questionnaire) ,[due diligence questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-meaning) (DDQs), and Q&A-style request for proposal (RFP) grids.
- **Decision 2, AutoRFP or Arphie:** both draft with citations. They split on pricing (published per-project plans vs a custom quote) and on how much of the AI's reasoning reviewers see.


## What gap do AutoRFP, Qvidian, and Arphie all leave open?


None of the three gives you AI-native drafting and finished proposal formatting in one tool, and none checks your source documents against each other.


- **Formatting vs AI:** Qvidian formats well but doesn't draft from live knowledge. AutoRFP and Arphie draft well but return answers into the buyer's file instead of building a designed proposal.
- **Contradictions between sources:** AutoRFP checks conflicts inside its own library, and Arphie's Smart Merge flags duplicates. Neither checks whether two of your documents disagree, which is how outdated certifications and wrong pricing tiers end up in submissions.

## Where do AutoRFP, Qvidian, and Arphie each win, and what do they cost you?


### AutoRFP: the fastest path off Qvidian, if your work is mostly questions


**Where it wins**


- **Questionnaire speed:** one G2 reviewer handling healthcare security questionnaires says work that took hours now takes minutes.
- **Answers you can check:** each draft carries a citation and a Trust Score, and answers go back into the buyer's Excel or Word file.
- **Bid screening:** Go/No-Go analysis scores each RFP against deal-breakers you set.


**What you give up**


- **Document craft:** it won't build a designed, 60-page proposal, and it doesn't publish a report builder like Qvidian's.
- **A clean start:** reviewers warn of a ramp-up period if your library is patchy, because the AI flags every inconsistency.


**Pick AutoRFP if:** questionnaires are most of your volume and you want a price before the first call.[AutoRFP pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/autorfp-pricing) runs $899/month for 24 projects a year or $1,299/month for 50, billed annually.


### Qvidian: still the best document factory, at a cost in upkeep


**Where it wins**


- **Formatted proposals:** templates and Office plug-ins turn approved content into polished, on-brand Word documents.
- **Reporting:** 70+ prebuilt reports and a report builder, which leadership in regulated industries often requires.
- **AI on top:** AI Assist adds generative drafting and[go/no-go](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/go-no-go-decision-projects) screening of incoming RFPs.


**What you give up**


- **Time:** reviewers describe content uploads and updates as slow and manual.
- **Ease:** the interface feels dated, and setup is heavy.
- **Budget flexibility:** every contributor needs a named seat, so bringing in 20 subject matter experts (SMEs) gets expensive fast.


**Pick Qvidian if:** you produce long, formatted proposals, leadership relies on reporting, and you have a content owner.[Qvidian pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/qvidian-pricing-features-reviews) is quote only, per named user, plus a year-one implementation fee.


### Arphie: the most honest AI, with the least predictable bill


**Where it wins**


- **Visible reasoning:** every answer shows the exact source, a confidence score, and why the AI answered that way, and it says so when sources can't support an answer.
- **Live sources:** drafts from Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Seismic, and Highspot, so answers change when your documents do.
- **Cleanup help:** Smart Merge surfaces duplicate entries.


**What you give up**


- **Track record:** founded in 2023, it has 26 G2 reviews, against Qvidian's 156.
- **Coverage:** a few G2 reviewers mention export issues, bugs, and no mobile app.
- **Predictable cost:**[Arphie pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/arphie-pricing-features-reviews) is a custom quote. Arphie earlier priced by concurrent projects at $36,000 to $60,000+ a year, which is hard to forecast if RFPs arrive in bursts, so confirm the current model.


**Pick Arphie if:** your reviewers won't sign off on AI answers they can't trace, and your volume is steady.


## Which pricing model costs more as you grow: AutoRFP, Qvidian, or Arphie?


Each model penalizes a different kind of growth, so work out which number in your business grows fastest before you compare quotes.


- **AutoRFP:** cost rises with how many RFPs you run.
- **Qvidian:** cost rises with how many people are involved.
- **Arphie:** cost has historically risen with how many RFPs overlap at once, since Arphie priced by concurrent projects; confirm its current model.


For a team running 40 RFPs a year with 25 contributors:


- **On AutoRFP:** 40 projects pushes you past Scale to Accelerate, at $15,588 a year, and the 25 people cost nothing extra.
- **On Qvidian:** all 25 contributors need named seats, plus implementation.
- **On Arphie:** the quote is custom, and under Arphie's earlier concurrent-project model, ten RFPs landing in one quarter would set the price.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can AutoRFP or Arphie import an existing Qvidian library?


Yes. Both import content from Excel and Word exports, and Arphie includes white-glove migration. Remove duplicates before the move so they don't carry over.


### How long does it take to switch off Qvidian?


Tool setup on AutoRFP or Arphie usually takes days to weeks. Most of the time goes to cleaning old content and setting permissions, so start well before your Qvidian renewal.


### Can a team keep Qvidian and add AutoRFP or Arphie?


Some do, keeping Qvidian for formatted proposals and adding an AI-native tool for questionnaires. That means two contracts and two content sources to keep in sync.


### Do AutoRFP, Qvidian, or Arphie offer a free trial?


AutoRFP lists a free trial on G2. Qvidian and Arphie sell through a demo and a custom quote.


### Do AutoRFP and Arphie train AI models on customer data?


Arphie says it doesn't use customer data to train models and runs zero data retention. AutoRFP says customer data isn't used to train public AI models.


### Which is best for investor relations DDQs: AutoRFP, Qvidian, or Arphie?


Arphie has a dedicated plan for investor relations teams, priced by seats and annual DDQ volume. AutoRFP and Qvidian handle DDQs within their standard plans.


### Which has the best customer support: AutoRFP, Qvidian, or Arphie?


AutoRFP's support is praised in 16 G2 reviews, Arphie's reviewers mention quick replies, and Qvidian publishes support hours for enterprise customers.
